summary.plain: LZ combined 280 live days of running and again saw no evidence of dark matter. The paper reports world-leading constraints on how weakly a dark matter particle (a WIMP) of 9 GeV/c² mass or more could interact with ordinary matter.
summary.technical: WS2024: total exposure 4.2 ± 0.1 tonne-years from 280 live days, of which 3.3 ± 0.1 tonne-years and 220 live days are new, combined with the 60-live-day WS2022 exposure. A technique to tag 214Pb β-decay backgrounds is used for the first time, and enhanced recombination in 124Xe two-neutrino double electron capture decays is a noteworthy new background. No evidence for an excess over expected backgrounds; the strongest spin-independent exclusion is 2.2e-48 cm² at 40 GeV/c² (90% CL) and the best spin-independent median sensitivity is 5.1e-48 cm².

title: Dark Matter Search Results from 4.2 Tonne-Years of Exposure of the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) Experiment
why_it_matters: The paper combines a new 220 live-day exposure (WS2024) with the 60 live-day exposure of the first LZ result (WS2022), for 4.2 tonne-years in total, and reports world-leading constraints on spin-independent and spin-dependent WIMP-nucleon cross sections for masses of 9 GeV/c² and above. It features 214Pb β-decay tagging for the first time and identifies a new 124Xe double-electron-capture background.
